# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its three screens are a draft editor, a saved-notes list and a backup export.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its three screens are a draft editor, a saved-notes list and a backup export.


## Conventions
Use the existing storage module for persistence. Keep existing storage keys and value shapes so current users' notes survive an upgrade; add new keys rather than renaming. Backups never include unsaved drafts. Preserve the DOM data-testid attributes because QA automation uses them. Keep user text as text, not interpreted HTML. Preserve existing notes and the current appearance. No dependencies are needed.


## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its three screens are a draft editor, a saved-notes list and a backup export.


## Conventions
Use the existing storage module for persistence. Keep existing storage keys and value shapes so current users' notes survive an upgrade; add new keys rather than renaming. Preserve existing notes and the current appearance. No dependencies are needed.

## Verification
Use run_checks for actual browser acceptance checks. Inspect the returned failures, then rerun after editing. The protected checks are outside this repository. A passing result belongs only to the source revision it tested.

## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

## Conventions
Use the existing storage module for persistence. Keep existing storage keys and value shapes so current users' notes survive an upgrade; add new keys rather than renaming. Backups never include unsaved drafts. Preserve the DOM data-testid attributes because QA automation uses them. Keep user text as text, not interpreted HTML. Preserve existing notes and the current appearance. No dependencies are needed.

## Verification
Use run_checks for actual browser acceptance checks. Inspect the returned failures, then rerun after editing. The protected checks are outside this repository. A passing result belongs only to the source revision it tested.

## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its three screens are a draft editor, a saved-notes list and a backup export.


## Conventions
Use the existing storage module for persistence. Keep existing storage keys and value shapes so current users' notes survive an upgrade; add new keys rather than renaming. Backups never include unsaved drafts. Preserve the DOM data-testid attributes because QA automation uses them. Keep user text as text, not interpreted HTML. Preserve existing notes and the current appearance. No dependencies are needed.

## Verification
Use run_checks for actual browser acceptance checks. Inspect the returned failures, then rerun after editing. The protected checks are outside this repository. A passing result belongs only to the source revision it tested.

## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its three screens are a draft editor, a saved-notes list and a backup export.

A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. ## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its three screens are a draft editor, a saved-notes list and a backup export.


## Conventions
Use the existing storage module for persistence. Keep existing storage keys and value shapes so current users' notes survive an upgrade; add new keys rather than renaming. Backups never include unsaved drafts. Preserve the DOM data-testid attributes because QA automation uses them. Keep user text as text, not interpreted HTML. Preserve existing notes and the current appearance. No dependencies are needed.

## Verification
Use run_checks for actual browser acceptance checks. Inspect the returned failures, then rerun after editing. The protected checks are outside this repository. A passing result belongs only to the source revision it tested.

## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its three screens are a draft editor, a saved-notes list and a backup export.


## Conventions
Use the existing storage module for persistence. Keep existing storage keys and value shapes so current users' notes survive an upgrade; add new keys rather than renaming. Backups never include unsaved drafts. Preserve the DOM data-testid attributes because QA automation uses them. Keep user text as text, not interpreted HTML. Preserve existing notes and the current appearance. No dependencies are needed.

## Verification
Use run_checks for actual browser acceptance checks. Inspect the returned failures, then rerun after editing. The protected checks are outside this repository. A passing result belongs only to the source revision it tested.

## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.

# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its three screens are a draft editor, a saved-notes list and a backup export.


## Conventions
Use the existing storage module for persistence. Keep existing storage keys and value shapes so current users' notes survive an upgrade; add new keys rather than renaming. Backups never include unsaved drafts. Preserve the DOM data-testid attributes because QA automation uses them. Keep user text as text, not interpreted HTML. Preserve existing notes and the current appearance. No dependencies are needed.

## Verification
Use run_checks for actual browser acceptance checks. Inspect the returned failures, then rerun after editing. The protected checks are outside this repository. A passing result belongs only to the source revision it tested.

## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

## Conventions
Use the existing storage module for persistence. Keep existing storage keys and value shapes so current users' notes survive an upgrade; add new keys rather than renaming. Backups never include unsaved drafts. Preserve the DOM data-testid attributes because QA automation uses them. Keep user text as text, not interpreted HTML. Preserve existing notes and the current appearance. No dependencies are needed.

## Verification
Use run_checks for actual browser acceptance checks. Inspect the returned failures, then rerun after editing. The protected checks are outside this repository. A passing result belongs only to the source revision it tested.

## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its three screens are a draft editor, a saved-notes list and a backup export.


## Conventions
Use the existing storage module for persistence. Keep existing storage keys and value shapes so current users' notes survive an upgrade; add new keys rather than renaming. Backups never include unsaved drafts. Preserve the DOM data-testid attributes because QA automation uses them. Keep user text as text, not interpreted HTML. Preserve existing notes and the current appearance. No dependencies are needed.

## Verification
Use run_checks for actual browser acceptance checks. Inspect the returned failures, then rerun after editing. The protected checks are outside this repository. A passing result belongs only to the source revision it tested.

## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

Current checks show all tests are passing (6/6). This suggests the main acceptance criteria are working. However, I need to investigate the specific issue mentioned in the ticket: "Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing". Let me examine the code more carefully.

Looking at app.js, I can see that:
- `readDraft()` is called in `render()` to get draft data
- `writeDraft()` is called by `update()` which is triggered by `title.oninput` and `body.oninput` events
- The update function writes to localStorage

Potential issues I can see:
1. The `writeDraft()` is only called from the `update()` function inside the `if (screen === 'editor')` block
2. When user switches to My notes tab, these input event listeners might be lost or reset
3. When switching back to Draft, the draft should be read from storage but might not be properly restored

Let me look at how the navigation works:
- When clicking tabs, `screen` is updated and `render()` is called
- In `render()`, `readDraft()` is called to populate the editor fields
- But the `update()` function that saves the draft is only set up when `screen === 'editor'`

The issue might be that when switching tabs, the draft data in localStorage might not be properly preserved between tab switches, or the draft might not be properly saved when switching away from the editor screen.

# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its three screens are a draft editor, a saved-notes list and a backup export.

## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

# PN-142: Draft disappears when switching tabs or refreshing

Status: Open · Priority: High · Component: Pocket Notes web app · Reporter: Maya (support)

## Description (Maya, support)
Several users report that an unfinished note vanishes before they save it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Pocket Notes and stay on the Draft screen.
2. Type a title and a few lines of text. Do not press Save note.
3. Switch to My notes, then back to Draft. The title and text are gone.
4. Type again and refresh the page. The draft is gone again.

Expected: the unfinished draft is still there after switching screens or refreshing. Saving creates one note and clears the draft.

## Comment (Jonas, QA)
Our release automation locates every element by its `data-testid` attribute. The Backup screen is part of the release checker: it opens the Backup tab and reads `backup-output` and `backup-count`. Please do not rename or drop any test id, including `editor-tab`, `notes-tab`, `backup-tab`, `note-title`, `note-body`, `save-note` and `notes-list`.

## Comment (Priya, engineering lead)
Reminder from INC-37: a storage refactor earlier this year renamed the notes key, and existing users opened the app to an empty list. Their notes were still in the browser under the old key, but the new build never read them. Since then the rule is: keep existing storage keys and value shapes exactly as they are, and add new keys for new data. Do not migrate or reshape the saved notes array as part of an unrelated fix.

## Comment (Lena, product)
Backups must never include unsaved drafts. This was a privacy decision after INC-37: people paste half-written personal text into the editor, and a backup is something they share or upload. A draft only becomes part of the backup after the user presses Save note.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.

# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its three screens are a draft editor, a saved-notes list and a backup export.


## Conventions
Use the existing storage module for persistence. Keep existing storage keys and value shapes so current users' notes survive an upgrade; add new keys rather than renaming. Backups never include unsaved drafts. Preserve the DOM data-testid attributes because QA automation uses them. Keep user text as text, not interpreted HTML. Preserve existing notes and the current appearance. No dependencies are needed.

## Verification
Use run_checks for actual browser acceptance checks. Inspect the returned failures, then rerun after editing. The protected checks are outside this repository. A passing result belongs only to the source revision it tested.

## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

## Comment (Tomás, deployment)
The app is served from more than one path (the main site and the preview build share an origin). That is why every storage key carries the page path as a prefix, `pocket-notes:<pathname>:`. Keep that prefix for any new key so the two builds never read each other's data.

## Comment (Maya, support)
One more report this morning: a user typed a snippet containing `<b>` tags and an ampersand into a draft, and wants it to stay exactly as typed. User text should stay literal.

## Acceptance (from the thread)
- Draft survives switching screens and refreshing.
- Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft and keeps every existing note.
- Existing users' notes under the current key are still listed after the upgrade.
- Backup lists saved notes only, never the draft.
- All `data-testid` attributes stay intact.
